# AI Assistant Interpretation — Request No. 2605363

## CRITICAL FLAGS / REVIEW POINTS
- **No primary (breast) tumour specimen in this report.** Only the right axillary dissection is documented; ypT category, margin status, and primary-tumour-bed parameters (residual invasive size, cellularity, %DCIS) are not available here, so the AJCC prognostic stage group and the RCB score cannot be independently verified from this document alone — RCB is a composite index requiring both primary-tumour-bed and nodal data.
- **RCB‑III is stated as the "treatment response index for this dissection"** — confirm that this value already incorporates the concurrently resected primary tumour bed (from a companion specimen/report) rather than being derived from nodal data in isolation.
- **Biomarker (ER/PR/HER2 ± Ki‑67) results are not reported here**; the comment defers to an unspecified "prior study" without citing values or accession number — creates a documentation gap for the current episode of care.
- **No orientation markers** on the macroscopic specimen limit anatomic-level mapping (I/II/III) of the 26 positive nodes; level III (infraclavicular) involvement cannot be confirmed or excluded from this report, which is relevant to definitive pN3a sub-classification.
- **Fat necrosis, foreign-body reaction, and cicatricial change** are noted — consistent with prior treatment effect but could obscure additional small metastatic foci; extent of sampling/levels examined per node not specified.
- No explicit statement regarding distant metastasis (M category); M0 is assumed pending clinical/radiologic correlation.

## SPECIMEN
Right axillary lymph node dissection, 50 nodes, post-neoadjuvant chemotherapy setting (residual cancer burden assessment).

## AI ASSISTANT'S PRELIMINARY DIAGNOSIS
Residual metastatic high-grade (nuclear grade 3) carcinoma, morphology consistent with invasive carcinoma of no special type (NST), in 26 of 50 right axillary lymph nodes, with extranodal (perinodal) extension and no evidence of pathologic treatment response — consistent with **ypN3a**, **RCB-III**.

## KEY FINDINGS
| Parameter | Finding |
|---|---|
| Nodal ratio | 26/50 positive (52%) |
| Largest metastatic deposit | 1 cm (macrometastasis, >2 mm) |
| Extranodal extension | Present, up to 5 mm into perinodal soft tissue |
| Nuclear grade | Grade 3 (high grade) in metastatic foci |
| Treatment response | None identified — non-responding nodal disease post-NAC |
| RCB class | RCB-III (per report, for this dissection) |
| Biomarker status | Not performed on current specimen; deferred to prior (unspecified) study. Not directly stated here — if correlation is required, a grade 3 tumour showing **no pathologic response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy** is statistically more consistent with a hormone receptor–positive/HER2-negative (luminal, high-grade) profile than with triple-negative or HER2-enriched disease, which more typically show higher pCR rates; this is an inference for correlation, not a confirmed result. |

## INTERPRETATION
Twenty-six of 50 axillary nodes (52% nodal ratio) harbour macrometastatic, grade 3 carcinoma with a largest deposit of 1 cm and extranodal extension up to 5 mm, with no morphologic evidence of chemotherapy-related change. Under AJCC 8th edition criteria, ≥10 positive axillary nodes with at least one deposit >2 mm satisfies **ypN3a**, independent of the presence of extranodal extension (ENE is not a formal N-modifier in the current breast staging schema but is a recognized adverse locoregional-recurrence risk factor and radiotherapy-planning consideration). Per the AJCC 8th edition anatomic staging table, any T category with N3/M0 corresponds to **anatomic Stage IIIC**; therefore, pending confirmation of M0 status and despite the primary tumour (ypT) not being documented in this specimen, the axillary findings alone are sufficient to place this case at a minimum of ypStage IIIC. Final AJCC *prognostic* stage grouping (which additionally weighs grade and ER/PR/HER2 status) cannot be finalized until the primary tumour bed report and confirmed biomarker profile are available.

The absence of any treatment effect in the nodal disease, combined with a high nodal burden and ENE, corresponds to **RCB-III**, the residual-disease category associated with the least favorable event-free and overall survival outcomes among the RCB classes, particularly when paired with HR+/HER2− or triple-negative biology. Taken together — ypN3a, extranodal extension, non-response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy, and RCB-III — this profile denotes extensive, high-grade, chemoresistant regional nodal disease with substantial risk for both locoregional recurrence (supporting regional nodal irradiation) and distant relapse, warranting consideration of escalated/alternative adjuvant systemic therapy once the confirmed receptor profile is available.

## RECOMMENDED CORRELATIONS AND STUDIES
- Correlate with the concurrent primary breast tumour resection specimen (ypT category, margins, residual cellularity, %in-situ component) to complete and validate the RCB calculation and finalize AJCC anatomic/prognostic staging.
- Retrieve and document the actual ER/PR/HER2 (and Ki‑67, if performed) results from the "prior study" referenced in the comment section, including report/accession identifier, for the permanent record of this episode.
- Consider re-testing biomarkers on the residual (post-NAC) tumour if there is any clinical suspicion of receptor discordance, per ASCO/CAP guidance for residual disease after neoadjuvant therapy.
- Correlate with the pretreatment core-biopsy report for baseline histologic subtype, grade, and biomarker status to assess pre-/post-NAC concordance.
- Clinical and imaging correlation to exclude infraclavicular (level III)/supraclavicular nodal disease and to formally establish M category for complete staging.
- Confirm total nodal yield/sampling adequacy and levels examined given the absence of orientation markers on the specimen.
- Multidisciplinary tumor board discussion regarding regional nodal irradiation (given ENE) and escalation of adjuvant systemic therapy (e.g., capecitabine, T-DM1, or CDK4/6 inhibition depending on confirmed receptor/HER2 status) in the context of RCB-III/non-response.

The post-neoadjuvant prefix (`yp`) is mandated given prior systemic therapy and formal treatment response evaluation.
  - **Extranodal Extension (ENE):** Significant extranodal tumor invasion extending up to 5 mm into perinodal adipose tissue is documented. Under AJCC 8th edition guidelines for breast cancer, ENE does not upstage the numeric ypN category, but extensive ENE (>2 mm) is recognized as a powerful independent adverse prognostic factor for locoregional recurrence and systemic failure.
  - **Overall Pathological Stage:** Under AJCC 8th edition anatomical staging rules, any T category with N3 disease in the absence of distant metastasis (cM0) corresponds to **ypStage IIIC** (ypT? ypN3a cM0).   - **Response Assessment:** No histologic signs of therapeutic response (tumor bed collapse, histiocytic replacement, or therapy-induced tumor necrosis) are observed within the evaluated lymph node metastases. Although the adjacent soft tissue demonstrates fat necrosis, foreign body reaction, and cicatricial change (reflecting prior biopsy/surgical disruption or peritumoral treatment effect), the viable tumor deposits exhibit complete resistance to neoadjuvant therapy.
  - **RCB Classification:** The dissection is classified as **RCB-III** (extensive residual disease).   - Immediate verification of the primary biopsy receptor profile is essential for clinical management.

anthropic/claude-fable-5-1.summary:
# Tumour Board Diagnostic Summary – Endometrial Pathology Report No. 2605694 (EN)

**Source:** `/app/attachments/report_2605694_EN.pdf` (single-page Anatomical Pathology Report – Histological Study; no images, no additional pages).
**Patient:** female, 47 years, outpatient. Admission 05/07/2026; report date 05/11/2026. Reporting pathologist: anonymised (pathologist–oncologist).
**Scope of available data:** the pathology report only. No clinical history, menopausal status, imaging, operative findings, tumour markers or family history are available. Nothing below that is stated as a fact goes beyond the report text; interpretive statements are labelled as such.

---

## 0. What the report actually contains (verbatim basis for every answer)

| Item | Report content |
|---|---|
| Specimens (labelled "RESECTION (3 SAMPLES)") | Block 1 "Endocervix": mucohemorrhagic material, combined volume 0.5 cc. Block 2 "Endometrium": mucohemorrhagic material, combined volume 3 cc. Block 3 "Endometrial polyps": multiple light-brown tissue fragments with raw surfaces, combined volume 1 cc. |
| Microscopic description | "See diagnosis" – no descriptive microscopy is given. |
| Diagnosis | "Endometrioid pattern endometrial adenocarcinoma, moderately differentiated, FIGO II, without evidence of vasculoneural invasion in this sample." "Some polypoid fragments with adenocarcinoma involvement." "No normal endocervix identified." "Scarce representation of basal endometrium." |
| Comments | Immunohistochemistry is **suggested** (not performed) on Block 3: Keratin cocktail, p53, p16, oestrogen receptor, progesterone receptor, beta-catenin, MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2. |
| Not mentioned anywhere | POLE testing; any IHC result; tumour size; myometrium; cervical stroma; adnexa; lymph nodes; background endometrium (hyperplasia/EIN); grading criteria used. |

**Nature of the material (interpretation):** although the laboratory header says "resection", the gross description (0.5 cc + 3 cc of fragmented mucohemorrhagic material plus 1 cc of polyp fragments) is that of endocervical/endometrial sampling (curettage/biopsy) with polypectomy. **No hysterectomy specimen, no myometrium, no cervical wall, no adnexa and no lymph nodes were received.** This single fact constrains most of the answers below.

---

## DIAGNOSIS

**Endometrioid endometrial adenocarcinoma ("endometrioid pattern"), moderately differentiated – FIGO grade 2**, diagnosed on the combined endocervical/endometrial/polyp samples, with explicit involvement of some of the endometrial polyp fragments (carcinoma involving endometrial polyp[s], Block 3). The report does not otherwise state the per-block distribution of tumour.

- Under the WHO Classification of Tumours, 5th edition (2020), FIGO grades 1–2 are grouped as **low-grade endometrioid carcinoma** (binary grading); grade 3 = high-grade. In FIGO 2023 terminology this is a "non-aggressive" histotype – *provided p53 proves wild-type* (see Molecular Subgroup).
- **Critical clarification for the board:** the "FIGO II" in the diagnostic line follows "moderately differentiated" and denotes the **FIGO grade (2)**, not a FIGO **stage II**. It must not be transcribed as stage II; nothing in a curettage specimen allows a stage to be assigned.
- Caveats on the diagnosis itself:
  - The histotype is a morphological call on fragmented material with no microscopic description and no confirmatory IHC. The panel the pathologist suggests is the appropriate one to (a) confirm endometrial rather than endocervical origin (ER/PR/p16 – relevant because an endocervical sample was submitted and "no normal endocervix identified"), (b) exclude a serous carcinoma with glandular/endometrioid-like morphology (p53, p16), and (c) complete the molecular classification (p53, MLH1/PMS2/MSH2/MSH6).
  - Grade assigned on preoperative sampling can be revised (usually upward) on the hysterectomy specimen; the criteria used (% solid non-squamous growth, nuclear grade) are not documented because the microscopic description was omitted.
  - Background endometrium (atypical hyperplasia/EIN) is not described; only "scarce representation of basal endometrium".

---

## FIGO STAGE

**Cannot be assigned from this specimen.** No FIGO stage – neither 2009 nor 2023 – can be given on curettage/polypectomy material, and the report itself does not state a stage.

Reasoning:
1. FIGO staging of endometrial carcinoma is surgico-pathological. Every stage-defining element is absent from this material: depth of myometrial invasion (no myometrium present; even the basal endometrium is "scarcely represented"), cervical stromal invasion, serosal/adnexal involvement, LVSI quantification, pelvic/para-aortic nodal status, peritoneal and distant disease.
2. **Cervical status is indeterminate.** "No normal endocervix identified" does not say whether the endocervical sample (Block 1, 0.5 cc) contained carcinoma or simply contained no evaluable endocervical mucosa. Even if tumour fragments were present in endocervical curettings, that would not establish cervical stromal invasion (FIGO 2009: endocervical glandular involvement only = stage I; stromal invasion is required for stage II) and could represent tumour dislodged from the cavity. Cervical stromal invasion can only be established on MRI and, definitively, on the hysterectomy specimen.
3. "FIGO II" in the report = grade 2 (see Diagnosis).
4. **Provisional clinical framing only (assumption, not a finding):** clinically presumed uterus-confined disease. If hysterectomy confirms a low-grade endometrioid carcinoma without extrauterine spread, the anatomical range would be FIGO 2023 stage IA1 (confined to polyp/endometrium) to IA2 (<50% myoinvasion, no/focal LVSI), IB (≥50%), IIA (cervical stroma) or IIB (substantial LVSI) – none of which is currently distinguishable. Under FIGO 2023 the molecular class also modifies stage (any stage I–II POLEmut → IAm POLEmut; p53abn with any myoinvasion → IICm p53abn), so the final stage requires **both** the hysterectomy with nodal assessment **and** the completed molecular classification.

---

## MOLECULAR SUBGROUP (WHO 5th edition integrated classification)

**Cannot be assigned from the available material – "molecular classification pending / not performed".**

- The WHO 5th edition (and ESGO–ESTRO–ESP 2025) integrated classification requires three analyses applied hierarchically: **POLE** exonuclease-domain pathogenic-variant testing → **MMR** protein IHC (MLH1, PMS2, MSH2, MSH6) → **p53** IHC; NSMP is the residual group when all three are normal. Multiple-classifier tumours are assigned by the genomic driver (POLEmut > MMRd > p53abn).
- In this report, p53 and the four MMR proteins were only **suggested** on Block 3; **no IHC result is reported**, and **POLE testing is not mentioned at all**. Therefore none of POLE-ultramutated, MMR-deficient, p53-abnormal or NSMP can be assigned, and NSMP must not be assumed by default (it is a diagnosis of exclusion).
- Why this is the single most consequential missing item for the board:
  - **p53abn** would move a "grade 2" tumour into the high-risk group if any myoinvasion is present (FIGO 2023 IICm p53abn; adjuvant chemo-radiotherapy).
  - **POLEmut** would confer an excellent prognosis with omission of adjuvant therapy at stage I–II (FIGO 2023 IAm POLEmut).
  - **MMRd** would trigger Lynch syndrome work-up (MLH1 promoter methylation if MLH1/PMS2 loss; genetic counselling/germline testing otherwise), is relevant at 47 years, and determines immunotherapy eligibility should the disease prove advanced or recur.
  - **NSMP** is further stratified by **ER status** (ESGO 2025: NSMP low-grade *and* ER-positive vs NSMP high-grade *or* ER-negative), which is why the suggested ER/PR stains matter beyond diagnosis; nuclear beta-catenin (CTNNB1) is an additional adverse marker in low-grade NSMP.
- ESGO 2025 explicitly encourages molecular testing on biopsy/curettage material, so the existing blocks (Block 3 ± Block 2) are appropriate for this work-up now, before surgery.

---

## LYMPHOVASCULAR INVASION

**Absent (not identified) in the sampled material.** Report wording: "without evidence of vasculoneural invasion in this sample" – i.e., neither vascular nor perineural invasion was seen.

Caveat (interpretation): LVSI cannot be excluded on curettage/polypectomy material because it is assessed at the invasive front within the myometrium of the hysterectomy specimen, where it must also be **quantified** (none / focal <5 vessels / substantial ≥5 vessels on at least one H&E slide). Substantial LVSI alone would change stage (FIGO 2023 IIB) and risk group (high-intermediate). Final LVSI status is therefore **pending the hysterectomy**; the pathologist's own qualifier "in this sample" acknowledges this.

---

## MYOMETRIAL INVASION

**Cannot be estimated – no myometrium is present in the specimen.**

- The material consists of fragmented mucohemorrhagic endometrial tissue and polyp fragments, with only "scarce representation of basal endometrium"; the endometrial–myometrial junction is not represented, so neither presence nor depth (<50% vs ≥50%) of invasion can be judged. Any percentage would be speculation.
- The involvement of polypoid fragments raises the possibility that part of the carcinoma arises within a polyp, but the diagnosis is issued for the combined samples and is not stated to be confined to the polyps, so confinement to a polyp (FIGO 2023 IA1) cannot be concluded.
- Depth must be assessed pre-operatively by contrast-enhanced pelvic MRI (or expert transvaginal ultrasound) and definitively on the hysterectomy specimen.

---

## KEY PROGNOSTIC FEATURES

**Established from the report (favourable so far):**
- Endometrioid histotype (non-aggressive histotype in FIGO 2023 terms, pending p53).
- FIGO grade 2 / moderately differentiated = low-grade endometrioid carcinoma (WHO binary grading).
- No lymphovascular or perineural invasion identified in the sampled material.
- Carcinoma involving endometrial polyp fragments – compatible with, but not proof of, an early lesion.
- Age 47 (ESGO 2025 lists age <60 and low grade as factors favouring omission of vaginal brachytherapy in intermediate-risk disease).

**Unknown or potentially unfavourable (drivers of current uncertainty):**
- **Molecular class unknown** (p53, MMR, POLE not done) – the dominant determinant of risk group and adjuvant therapy; a p53abn result would convert this into high-risk disease.
- **ER/PR and beta-catenin status unknown** – ER negativity or nuclear beta-catenin (CTNNB1 mutation) worsen prognosis within NSMP low-grade tumours; ER also predicts endocrine responsiveness.
- **Depth of myometrial invasion unknown** (no myometrium sampled).
- **Cervical stromal involvement unknown** ("no normal endocervix identified"; tumour presence in Block 1 not stated).
- **LVSI status not definitively assessable** on curettage.
- **Tumour size, nodal status, adnexal/serosal/peritoneal status unknown** – no imaging or surgical data in the file.
- **Lynch syndrome risk unassessed** – MMR IHC pending in a patient aged <50.
- **Specimen/report limitations:** small volumes (0.5 cc, 3 cc, 1 cc); "See diagnosis" in place of a microscopic description; grading criteria, per-block tumour distribution and background endometrium undocumented; preoperative grade may change on hysterectomy.

---

## RECOMMENDED MANAGEMENT

Because neither stage nor molecular subgroup is established, definitive adjuvant recommendations cannot yet be made; the recommended pathway is to close the data gaps and then apply the ESGO–ESTRO–ESP 2025 molecular-integrated risk groups (which use FIGO 2023 staging). Recommendations are framed accordingly.

### 1. Complete the pathology work-up on the existing blocks (before surgery)
- **Perform** – not merely suggest – the recommended IHC panel on Block 3 (± Block 2 if tumour is better represented): p53, MLH1, PMS2, MSH2, MSH6, ER, PR, p16, beta-catenin, keratin cocktail. ESGO 2025: molecular classification should be done for all endometrial carcinomas; ER IHC is recommended in all cases; MMR IHC (two- or four-antibody approach) is the preferred Lynch pre-screen for every patient.
- **Add POLE exonuclease-domain testing** covering the 11 pathogenic variants (not in the suggested panel). It may be omitted only if final pathology places the tumour in a low-risk stage I category where it would not alter adjuvant treatment; given that stage, myoinvasion, LVSI and p53 status are all unknown, request it now or ensure it can be added promptly.
- If MLH1 (± PMS2) loss → MLH1 promoter hypermethylation testing; if unmethylated, or if MSH2/MSH6/isolated PMS2 loss → genetic counselling and germline testing (Lynch syndrome). Equivocal MMR IHC → MSI-PCR; equivocal p53 → TP53 sequencing.
- Request a **pathology addendum**: full microscopic description; per-block findings (specifically whether Block 1 endocervical material contains carcinoma or is non-representative); grading criteria (% solid growth, nuclear grade); background atypical hyperplasia/EIN; synoptic (ICCR/CAP) biopsy format; explicit statement that "FIGO II" means grade 2.
- Retain blocks for correlation; molecular testing need only be repeated on the hysterectomy specimen if biopsy tissue is scant/equivocal or a new tumour component appears.

### 2. Pre-treatment clinical staging
- Contrast-enhanced **pelvic MRI** (or expert transvaginal ultrasound) for depth of myometrial invasion, **cervical stromal invasion** (specifically indicated here because cervical status is indeterminate), adnexa and pelvic nodes.
- Chest imaging; CT chest/abdomen/pelvis if MRI shows deep invasion/cervical or extrauterine disease or if high-risk features emerge (e.g., p53abn, high grade on review). Serum CA-125 optional.
- Clinical assessment: pelvic/speculum examination for cervical or vaginal extension, menopausal status, BMI, comorbidities and surgical fitness, personal/family cancer history (Lynch).

### 3. Primary treatment (fit patient, presumed uterus-confined disease)
- **Total hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy** by a **minimally invasive approach**, avoiding any intraperitoneal tumour spillage or morcellation; peritoneal survey. Omentectomy is not required for endometrioid histology (would be reconsidered only if IHC reclassifies the tumour as serous/undifferentiated).
- **Sentinel lymph node biopsy** (indocyanine green, cervical injection) with pathological ultrastaging in all presumed uterus-confined disease; if no SLN is detected on a side, side-specific systematic lymphadenectomy for high-intermediate/high-risk disease and can be considered for presumed intermediate risk; not needed for low-risk disease.
- If cervical stromal involvement is confirmed: simple total hysterectomy with free margins remains standard; more extensive (radical) procedures only if required to achieve free margins.
- **Ovarian preservation:** not routinely recommended here – ESGO 2025 criteria are premenopausal age <45 years, FIGO 2023 IA1/IA2 and low risk by molecular classification, with bilateral salpingectomy, and never in Lynch/BRCA carriers. At 47 with molecular and myoinvasion status unknown, BSO is the standard; discuss only after MDT review if the patient is premenopausal and strongly requests it.
- **Fertility-sparing (progestin) treatment:** not applicable as standard care – reserved for grade 1 endometrioid carcinoma without myometrial invasion on imaging in patients wishing to conceive; this tumour is grade 2 and myoinvasion is unassessed.
- If medically unfit for surgery: definitive radiotherapy (image-guided intrauterine brachytherapy alone can be considered for low-grade tumours without deep invasion; EBRT + brachytherapy otherwise).

### 4. Adjuvant therapy – to be decided after final surgical pathology + molecular class (ESGO–ESTRO–ESP 2025 risk groups)
| Final finding (this grade-2 endometrioid tumour) | Risk group | Adjuvant recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| **POLEmut**, any stage I–II (→ IAm POLEmut) | Low | No adjuvant therapy |
| **MMRd or NSMP low-grade ER-positive**, no or <50% myoinvasion, no/focal LVSI (IA1/IA2) | Low | No adjuvant therapy (observation) |

{"filePath": "/app/response.md", "content": "# Tumour Board Diagnostic Summary – Endometrial Pathology Report No. 2605694 (EN)

**Source:** `/app/attachments/report_2605694_EN.pdf` (single-page Anatomical Pathology Report – Histological Study; no images, no additional pages).
**Patient:** female, 47 years, outpatient. Admission 05/07/2026; report date 05/11/2026. Reporting pathologist: anonymised (pathologist–oncologist).
**Scope of available data:** the pathology report only. No clinical history, menopausal status, imaging, operative findings, tumour markers or family history are available. Nothing below that is stated as a fact goes beyond the report text; interpretive statements are labelled as such.

---

## 0. What the report actually contains (verbatim basis for every answer)

| Item | Report content |
|---|---|
| Specimens (labelled "RESECTION (3 SAMPLES)") | Block 1 "Endocervix": mucohemorrhagic material, combined volume 0.5 cc. Block 2 "Endometrium": mucohemorrhagic material, combined volume 3 cc. Block 3 "Endometrial polyps": multiple light-brown tissue fragments with raw surfaces, combined volume 1 cc. |
| Microscopic description | "See diagnosis" – no descriptive microscopy is given. |
| Diagnosis | "Endometrioid pattern endometrial adenocarcinoma, moderately differentiated, FIGO II, without evidence of vasculoneural invasion in this sample." "Some polypoid fragments with adenocarcinoma involvement." "No normal endocervix identified." "Scarce representation of basal endometrium." |
| Comments | Immunohistochemistry is **suggested** (not performed) on Block 3: Keratin cocktail, p53, p16, oestrogen receptor, progesterone receptor, beta-catenin, MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2. |
| Not mentioned anywhere | POLE testing; any IHC result; tumour size; myometrium; cervical stroma; adnexa; lymph nodes; background endometrium (hyperplasia/EIN); grading criteria used. |

**Nature of the material (interpretation):** although the laboratory header says "resection", the gross description (0.5 cc + 3 cc of fragmented mucohemorrhagic material plus 1 cc of polyp fragments) is that of endocervical/endometrial sampling (curettage/biopsy) with polypectomy. **No hysterectomy specimen, no myometrium, no cervical wall, no adnexa and no lymph nodes were received.** This single fact constrains most of the answers below.

---

## DIAGNOSIS

**Endometrioid endometrial adenocarcinoma ("endometrioid pattern"), moderately differentiated – FIGO grade 2**, involving the endometrial sample and some of the endometrial polyp fragments (carcinoma involving endometrial polyp[s], Block 3).

- Under the WHO Classification of Tumours, 5th edition (2020), FIGO grades 1–2 are grouped as **low-grade endometrioid carcinoma** (binary grading); grade 3 = high-grade. In FIGO 2023 terminology this is a "non-aggressive" histotype – *provided p53 proves wild-type* (see Molecular Subgroup).
- **Critical clarification for the board:** the "FIGO II" in the diagnostic line follows "moderately differentiated" and denotes the **FIGO grade (2)**, not a FIGO **stage II**. It must not be transcribed as stage II; nothing in a curettage specimen allows a stage to be assigned.
- Caveats on the diagnosis itself:
  - The histotype is a morphological call on fragmented material with no microscopic description and no confirmatory IHC. The panel the pathologist suggests is the appropriate one to (a) confirm endometrial rather than endocervical origin (ER/PR/p16 – relevant because an endocervical sample was submitted and "no normal endocervix identified"), (b) exclude a serous carcinoma with glandular/endometrioid-like morphology (p53, p16), and (c) complete the molecular classification (p53, MLH1/PMS2/MSH2/MSH6).
  - Grade assigned on preoperative sampling can be revised (usually upward) on the hysterectomy specimen; the criteria used (% solid non-squamous growth, nuclear grade) are not documented because the microscopic description was omitted.
  - Background endometrium (atypical hyperplasia/EIN) is not described; only "scarce representation of basal endometrium".

---

## FIGO STAGE

**Cannot be assigned from this specimen.** No FIGO stage – neither 2009 nor 2023 – can be given on curettage/polypectomy material, and the report itself does not state a stage.

Reasoning:
1. FIGO staging of endometrial carcinoma is surgico-pathological. Every stage-defining element is absent from this material: depth of myometrial invasion (no myometrium present; even the basal endometrium is "scarcely represented"), cervical stromal invasion, serosal/adnexal involvement, LVSI quantification, pelvic/para-aortic nodal status, peritoneal and distant disease.
2. **Cervical status is indeterminate.** "No normal endocervix identified" does not say whether the endocervical sample (Block 1, 0.5 cc) contained carcinoma or simply contained no evaluable endocervical mucosa. Even if tumour fragments were present in endocervical curettings, that would not establish cervical stromal invasion (FIGO 2009: endocervical glandular involvement only = stage I; stromal invasion is required for stage II) and could represent tumour dislodged from the cavity. Cervical stromal invasion can only be established on MRI and, definitively, on the hysterectomy specimen.
3. "FIGO II" in the report = grade 2 (see Diagnosis).
4. **Provisional clinical framing only (assumption, not a finding):** clinically presumed uterus-confined disease. If hysterectomy confirms a low-grade endometrioid carcinoma without extrauterine spread, the anatomical range would be FIGO 2023 stage IA1 (confined to polyp/endometrium) to IA2 (<50% myoinvasion, no/focal LVSI), IB (≥50%), IIA (cervical stroma) or IIB (substantial LVSI) – none of which is currently distinguishable. Under FIGO 2023 the molecular class also modifies stage (any stage I–II POLEmut → IAm POLEmut; p53abn with any myoinvasion → IICm p53abn), so the final stage requires **both** the hysterectomy with nodal assessment **and** the completed molecular classification.

---

## MOLECULAR SUBGROUP (WHO 5th edition integrated classification)

**Cannot be assigned from the available material – "molecular classification pending / not performed".**

- The WHO 5th edition (and ESGO–ESTRO–ESP 2025) integrated classification requires three analyses applied hierarchically: **POLE** exonuclease-domain pathogenic-variant testing → **MMR** protein IHC (MLH1, PMS2, MSH2, MSH6) → **p53** IHC; NSMP is the residual group when all three are normal. Multiple-classifier tumours are assigned by the genomic driver (POLEmut > MMRd > p53abn).
- In this report, p53 and the four MMR proteins were only **suggested** on Block 3; **no IHC result is reported**, and **POLE testing is not mentioned at all**. Therefore none of POLE-ultramutated, MMR-deficient, p53-abnormal or NSMP can be assigned, and NSMP must not be assumed by default (it is a diagnosis of exclusion).
- Why this is the single most consequential missing item for the board:
  - **p53abn** would move a "grade 2" tumour into the high-risk group if any myoinvasion is present (FIGO 2023 IICm p53abn; adjuvant chemo-radiotherapy).
  - **POLEmut** would confer an excellent prognosis with omission of adjuvant therapy at stage I–II (FIGO 2023 IAm POLEmut).
  - **MMRd** would trigger Lynch syndrome work-up (MLH1 promoter methylation if MLH1/PMS2 loss; genetic counselling/germline testing otherwise), is relevant at 47 years, and determines immunotherapy eligibility should the disease prove advanced or recur.
  - **NSMP** is further stratified by **ER status** (ESGO 2025: NSMP low-grade *and* ER-positive vs NSMP high-grade *or* ER-negative), which is why the suggested ER/PR stains matter beyond diagnosis; nuclear beta-catenin (CTNNB1) is an additional adverse marker in low-grade NSMP.
- ESGO 2025 explicitly encourages molecular testing on biopsy/curettage material, so the existing blocks (Block 3 ± Block 2) are appropriate for this work-up now, before surgery.

---

## LYMPHOVASCULAR INVASION

**Absent (not identified) in the sampled material.** Report wording: "without evidence of vasculoneural invasion in this sample" – i.e., neither vascular nor perineural invasion was seen.

Caveat (interpretation): LVSI cannot be excluded on curettage/polypectomy material because it is assessed at the invasive front within the myometrium of the hysterectomy specimen, where it must also be **quantified** (none / focal <5 vessels / substantial ≥5 vessels on at least one H&E slide). Substantial LVSI alone would change stage (FIGO 2023 IIB) and risk group (high-intermediate). Final LVSI status is therefore **pending the hysterectomy**; the pathologist's own qualifier "in this sample" acknowledges this.

---

## MYOMETRIAL INVASION

**Cannot be estimated – no myometrium is present in the specimen.**

- The material consists of fragmented mucohemorrhagic endometrial tissue and polyp fragments, with only "scarce representation of basal endometrium"; the endometrial–myometrial junction is not represented, so neither presence nor depth (<50% vs ≥50%) of invasion can be judged. Any percentage would be speculation.
- The involvement of polypoid fragments raises the possibility that part of the carcinoma arises within a polyp, but the diagnosis also covers the "Endometrium" sample, so confinement to a polyp (FIGO 2023 IA1) cannot be concluded.
- Depth must be assessed pre-operatively by contrast-enhanced pelvic MRI (or expert transvaginal ultrasound) and definitively on the hysterectomy specimen.

---

## KEY PROGNOSTIC FEATURES

**Established from the report (favourable so far):**
- Endometrioid histotype (non-aggressive histotype in FIGO 2023 terms, pending p53).
- FIGO grade 2 / moderately differentiated = low-grade endometrioid carcinoma (WHO binary grading).
- No lymphovascular or perineural invasion identified in the sampled material.
- Carcinoma involving endometrial polyp fragments – compatible with, but not proof of, an early lesion.
- Age 47 (ESGO 2025 lists age <60 and low grade as factors favouring omission of vaginal brachytherapy in intermediate-risk disease).

**Unknown or potentially unfavourable (drivers of current uncertainty):**
- **Molecular class unknown** (p53, MMR, POLE not done) – the dominant determinant of risk group and adjuvant therapy; a p53abn result would convert this into high-risk disease.
- **ER/PR and beta-catenin status unknown** – ER negativity or nuclear beta-catenin (CTNNB1 mutation) worsen prognosis within NSMP low-grade tumours; ER also predicts endocrine responsiveness.
- **Depth of myometrial invasion unknown** (no myometrium sampled).
- **Cervical stromal involvement unknown** ("no normal endocervix identified"; tumour presence in Block 1 not stated).
- **LVSI status not definitively assessable** on curettage.
- **Tumour size, nodal status, adnexal/serosal/peritoneal status unknown** – no imaging or surgical data in the file.
- **Lynch syndrome risk unassessed** – MMR IHC pending in a patient aged <50.
- **Specimen/report limitations:** small volumes (0.5 cc, 3 cc, 1 cc); "See diagnosis" in place of a microscopic description; grading criteria, per-block tumour distribution and background endometrium undocumented; preoperative grade may change on hysterectomy.

---

## RECOMMENDED MANAGEMENT

Because neither stage nor molecular subgroup is established, definitive adjuvant recommendations cannot yet be made; the recommended pathway is to close the data gaps and then apply the ESGO–ESTRO–ESP 2025 molecular-integrated risk groups (which use FIGO 2023 staging). Recommendations are framed accordingly.

### 1. Complete the pathology work-up on the existing blocks (before surgery)
- **Perform** – not merely suggest – the recommended IHC panel on Block 3 (± Block 2 if tumour is better represented): p53, MLH1, PMS2, MSH2, MSH6, ER, PR, p16, beta-catenin, keratin cocktail. ESGO 2025: molecular classification should be done for all endometrial carcinomas; ER IHC is recommended in all cases; MMR IHC (two- or four-antibody approach) is the preferred Lynch pre-screen for every patient.
- **Add POLE exonuclease-domain testing** covering the 11 pathogenic variants (not in the suggested panel). It may be omitted only if final pathology places the tumour in a low-risk stage I category where it would not alter adjuvant treatment; given that stage, myoinvasion, LVSI and p53 status are all unknown, request it now or ensure it can be added promptly.
- If MLH1 (± PMS2) loss → MLH1 promoter hypermethylation testing; if unmethylated, or if MSH2/MSH6/isolated PMS2 loss → genetic counselling and germline testing (Lynch syndrome). Equivocal MMR IHC → MSI-PCR; equivocal p53 → TP53 sequencing.
- Request a **pathology addendum**: full microscopic description; per-block findings (specifically whether Block 1 endocervical material contains carcinoma or is non-representative); grading criteria (% solid growth, nuclear grade); background atypical hyperplasia/EIN; synoptic (ICCR/CAP) biopsy format; explicit statement that "FIGO II" means grade 2.
- Retain blocks for correlation; molecular testing need only be repeated on the hysterectomy specimen if biopsy tissue is scant/equivocal or a new tumour component appears.

### 2. Pre-treatment clinical staging
- Contrast-enhanced **pelvic MRI** (or expert transvaginal ultrasound) for depth of myometrial invasion, **cervical stromal invasion** (specifically indicated here because cervical status is indeterminate), adnexa and pelvic nodes.
- Chest imaging; CT chest/abdomen/pelvis if MRI shows deep invasion/cervical or extrauterine disease or if high-risk features emerge (e.g., p53abn, high grade on review). Serum CA-125 optional.
- Clinical assessment: pelvic/speculum examination for cervical or vaginal extension, menopausal status, BMI, comorbidities and surgical fitness, personal/family cancer history (Lynch).

### 3. Primary treatment (fit patient, presumed uterus-confined disease)
- **Total hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy** by a **minimally invasive approach**, avoiding any intraperitoneal tumour spillage or morcellation; peritoneal survey. Omentectomy is not required for endometrioid histology (would be reconsidered only if IHC reclassifies the tumour as serous/undifferentiated).
- **Sentinel lymph node biopsy** (indocyanine green, cervical injection) with pathological ultrastaging in all presumed uterus-confined disease; if no SLN is detected on a side, side-specific systematic lymphadenectomy for high-intermediate/high-risk disease and can be considered for presumed intermediate risk; not needed for low-risk disease.
- If cervical stromal involvement is confirmed: simple total hysterectomy with free margins remains standard; more extensive (radical) procedures only if required to achieve free margins.
- **Ovarian preservation:** not routinely recommended here – ESGO 2025 criteria are premenopausal age <45 years, FIGO 2023 IA1/IA2 and low risk by molecular classification, with bilateral salpingectomy, and never in Lynch/BRCA carriers. At 47 with molecular and myoinvasion status unknown, BSO is the standard; discuss only after MDT review if the patient is premenopausal and strongly requests it.
- **Fertility-sparing (progestin) treatment:** not applicable as standard care – reserved for grade 1 endometrioid carcinoma without myometrial invasion on imaging in patients wishing to conceive; this tumour is grade 2 and myoinvasion is unassessed.
- If medically unfit for surgery: definitive radiotherapy (image-guided intrauterine brachytherapy alone can be considered for low-grade tumours without deep invasion; EBRT + brachytherapy otherwise).

### 4. Adjuvant therapy – to be decided after final surgical pathology + molecular class (ESGO–ESTRO–ESP 2025 risk groups)
| Final finding (this grade-2 endometrioid tumour) | Risk group | Adjuvant recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| **POLEmut**, any stage I–II (→ IAm POLEmut) | Low | No adjuvant therapy |
| **MMRd or NSMP low-grade ER-positive**, no or <50% myoinvasion, no/focal LVSI (IA1/IA2) | Low | No adjuvant therapy (observation) |
| **MMRd or NSMP low-grade ER-positive**, ≥50% myoinvasion, no/focal LVSI (IB); **NSMP low-grade ER-positive** with cervical stromal invasion (IIA) | Intermediate | Vaginal brachytherapy should be considered; no adjuvant therapy is an option, especially age <60 (applies at 47) or low grade |
| **MMRd** with cervical stromal invasion (IIA); **MMRd or NSMP low-grade ER-positive** with substantial LVSI (IIB) | High-intermediate | EBRT recommended; vaginal brachytherapy alternative if SLN/nodal staging pN0; no adjuvant therapy can be considered if pN0, no substantial LVSI and low grade |
| **p53abn** with any myoinvasion (IICm p53abn), or **NSMP ER-negative** with myoinvasion (IA2/IB) or stage II | High | EBRT with concurrent and adjuvant chemotherapy (carboplatin–paclitaxel) or sequential chemo-radiotherapy; chemotherapy ± brachytherapy alternative |
| **p53abn or NSMP ER-negative** confined to polyp/endometrium, no myoinvasion (IA1) | Uncertain | Adjuvant therapy generally not recommended; MDT discussion |
| Stage III–IVA (nodes, adnexa, serosa, vagina/parametria, peritoneum), MMRd/NSMP/p53abn | High | Chemo-radiotherapy or chemotherapy; for **MMRd** stage III–IVA, chemotherapy combined with an immune checkpoint inhibitor (± EBRT) should be considered |
| Unresectable/residual/metastatic disease | Advanced | MMRd: carboplatin–paclitaxel + checkpoint inhibitor (dostarlimab, durvalumab or pembrolizumab) then ICI maintenance; non-MMRd: carboplatin–paclitaxel (± ICI); low-grade ER-positive, low-volume/indolent disease: endocrine therapy (progestins preferred; aromatase inhibitors/tamoxifen alternatives) |

### 5. Hereditary risk, follow-up and survivorship
- Universal Lynch pre-screening by MMR IHC (with MLH1 methylation where indicated) and genetic counselling if abnormal or if family history is suggestive – particularly pertinent at 47 years.
- Risk-adapted, personalised follow-up per ESGO 2025 (informed by final molecular class and treatment); patient education on recurrence symptoms (vaginal bleeding), menopause management after BSO, lifestyle counselling, psycho-oncological support, and consideration of clinical-trial enrolment (e.g., molecularly stratified adjuvant trials).
- **Re-present at tumour board** (a) once IHC ± POLE results are available and MRI is done, to finalise the surgical plan, and (b) after final hysterectomy/SLN pathology, to assign the definitive FIGO 2023 stage with molecular annotation and the adjuvant strategy.

---

## Bottom line for the board

Low-grade (FIGO grade 2, moderately differentiated) endometrioid endometrial adenocarcinoma diagnosed on endocervical/endometrial curettage and polypectomy material (Request 2605694, 47-year-old woman), with carcinoma involving endometrial polyp fragments and **no lymphovascular or perineural invasion in the sample**. **FIGO stage, depth of myometrial invasion, cervical stromal status and molecular subgroup are all not assessable from this specimen** – the "FIGO II" in the report is the grade, not the stage, and the recommended IHC (p53, MMR proteins, ER, PR, p16, beta-catenin, keratin cocktail) has not yet been performed; POLE testing has not been requested. Recommended next steps: perform IHC + POLE on the existing blocks, pelvic MRI, then total hysterectomy with BSO and sentinel lymph node biopsy (minimally invasive), followed by adjuvant therapy assigned strictly by the ESGO–ESTRO–ESP 2025 molecular-integrated risk group once the final stage and molecular class are known.

# Tumour Board Diagnostic Summary: Endometrial Carcinoma

**Report:** `report_2605694_EN.pdf`, Anatomical Pathology Report (Histological Study), Request No. 2605694
**Patient:** female, 47 years, outpatient. Admission 05/07/2026; report date 05/11/2026 (dates as printed).
**Evidence base:** this one-page report is the only source. No imaging, operative, IHC/molecular, family-history or other clinical data were provided. I used FIGO 2023, the WHO 5th edition classification and the ESGO-ESTRO-ESP 2025 guidelines only to interpret the report and to frame recommendations. Nothing from those sources is presented as a finding in this patient.

## Report findings (as documented)

| Block | Label | Macroscopic description |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | "Endocervix" | Mucohemorrhagic material, combined volume 0.5 cc |
| 2 | "Endometrium" | Mucohemorrhagic material, combined volume 3 cc |
| 3 | "Endometrial polyps" | Multiple light brown tissue fragments with raw surfaces, combined volume 1 cc |

- **Microscopic description:** "See diagnosis." There is no separate microscopic text.
- **Diagnosis** (one combined diagnosis under "ENDOCERVIX, ENDOMETRIUM, ENDOMETRIAL POLYPS, RESECTION (3 SAMPLES)"):
  - "Endometrioid pattern endometrial adenocarcinoma, moderately differentiated, FIGO II, without evidence of vasculoneural invasion in this sample"
  - "Some polypoid fragments with adenocarcinoma involvement"
  - "No normal endocervix identified"
  - "Scarce representation of basal endometrium"
- **Comment:** immunohistochemistry is *suggested* on Block 3: Keratin Cocktail, P53, P16, Estrogen Receptors, Progesterone Receptors, Beta-Catenin, MLH1, MSH2, MSH6 and PMS2. **No IHC results are reported, and no addendum was provided.**

> **Key interpretive points**
> 1. **"FIGO II" is the FIGO grade, not the FIGO stage.** It appears next to "moderately differentiated", which means FIGO grade 2. It does not mean stage II.
> 2. **The specimen is fragmented resection/curettage material, not a hysterectomy.** A surgical stage and the depth of myometrial invasion cannot be derived from it.
> 3. **IHC was only recommended, so the molecular subgroup cannot be assigned.** POLE testing was not requested at all.
> 4. **"No normal endocervix identified" means the endocervical sample is not representative, so cervical status is unknown.** This finding is *not* evidence of cervical stromal invasion.

---

## DIAGNOSIS:
**Endometrioid adenocarcinoma of the endometrium, FIGO grade 2 (moderately differentiated).** Under FIGO 2023, grade 1–2 endometrioid carcinoma is low grade and counts as a "non-aggressive" histological type.

- Adenocarcinoma involves some of the polypoid (endometrial polyp) fragments.
- Other statements in the report:
  - no vasculoneural invasion in this sample
  - no normal endocervix identified
  - scarce basal endometrium
- **Limitations:**
  - There is no microscopic description. The architectural basis for grade 2 is therefore not documented. By FIGO definition, grade 2 means 6–50% solid non-squamous, non-morular growth.
  - Apart from the polyp fragments, the report does not say which of the three samples contain carcinoma.
  - The suggested p53/p16/ER/PR panel would also help confirm the endometrioid histotype and an endometrial rather than endocervical origin. This matters because no normal endocervix was identified.
  - Histotype and grade should be confirmed on the hysterectomy specimen.

## FIGO STAGE:
**Cannot be assigned from the available material. The surgical-pathological FIGO stage is undetermined, and no "most likely" stage can responsibly be named from this specimen.**

Reasons:
1. **"FIGO II" does not mean stage II.** In the report it follows "moderately differentiated" and describes FIGO grade 2. Recording stage II would wrongly imply cervical stromal invasion and could lead to overtreatment, such as radical surgery or radiotherapy.
2. **FIGO staging (2009 and 2023) is surgical-pathological.** It needs hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy (BSO) and nodal staging to define:
   - depth of myometrial invasion
   - cervical stromal invasion
   - extent of lymphovascular space invasion (LVSI): focal, or substantial (≥5 vessels)
   - adnexal, serosal, nodal and peritoneal status

   FIGO 2023 also builds in histotype, grade, LVSI and molecular class (e.g., IAm POLEmut, IICm p53abn). None of this information is available.
3. **Cervical involvement is neither shown nor excluded.**
   - No normal endocervix was identified.
   - The report does not state that carcinoma is present in the "Endocervix" sample.
   - Carcinoma fragments in an endocervical sample could be displaced tumour from the uterine body. They would not prove cervical *stromal* invasion, which is the only cervical finding that defines stage II (FIGO 2023 IIA). Under FIGO 2009, involvement of endocervical glands alone is still stage I.
4. **What can be said:**
   - Carcinoma involves the endometrium and endometrial polyps.
   - No reported finding documents cervical stromal invasion, substantial LVSI or disease outside the uterus.
   - This is *compatible with* stage I but does not establish it.
   - For a low-grade endometrioid tumour, the final FIGO 2023 stage could be anything from IA1 (confined to a polyp or the endometrium) through IA2, IB, IIA and IIB to III–IV. It would carry a molecular annotation, e.g., IAm POLEmut, or IICm p53abn if the tumour is p53-abnormal with any myometrial invasion.

## MOLECULAR SUBGROUP (WHO 5th edition integrated classification):
**Cannot be assigned from the available material.** IHC (p53, MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2 and the rest of the panel) was only suggested on Block 3; it was not performed or reported. POLE mutation analysis was not requested.

- None of the four subgroups (POLE-ultramutated, MMR-deficient, p53-abnormal, NSMP) can be named.
- **NSMP must not be assigned by default.** It is a diagnosis of exclusion that requires POLE wild-type, MMR-proficient and p53 wild-type results.
- Low-grade endometrioid morphology does not predict the subgroup; all four subgroups can look like this.
- **Tests needed to classify:**
  - p53 IHC
  - MMR IHC (MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2), with reflex MLH1 promoter methylation testing if MLH1 or MLH1/PMS2 expression is lost
  - **POLE exonuclease-domain sequencing covering all 11 pathogenic variants.** This is not in the suggested panel and cannot be done by IHC.
  - If more than one classifier is abnormal, classify by the genomic driver: POLEmut takes precedence over MMRd, and MMRd over p53abn.
- **Supporting biomarkers (refine prognosis but do not define the subgroup):**
  - ER status: ESGO-ESTRO-ESP 2025 splits NSMP into "low-grade and ER-positive" versus "high-grade and/or ER-negative".
  - Nuclear β-catenin: a surrogate for CTNNB1 mutation and an adverse factor within low-grade NSMP.

## LYMPHOVASCULAR INVASION:
**Absent: not identified in this sample.** The report says "without evidence of vasculoneural invasion in this sample". "Vasculoneural" covers lymphovascular and perineural invasion.

- **This finding is provisional.** It is based on small fragments without myometrium or the tumour–myometrium interface, which is where LVSI is usually seen.
- Definitive LVSI status and its extent (none, focal, or substantial = ≥5 vessels by WHO criteria) must be assessed on the hysterectomy. Substantial LVSI would upstage a low-grade endometrioid tumour to FIGO 2023 IIB.

## MYOMETRIAL INVASION:
**Not assessable. The depth cannot be estimated from this specimen.**

- None of the three samples is described as containing myometrium.
- The report explicitly notes "scarce representation of basal endometrium", so even the endometrial–myometrial junction is barely sampled.
- As a result, none of these categories can be inferred:
  - no invasion (IA1)
  - invasion of less than 50% (IA2)
  - invasion of 50% or more (IB)
- **Absence of invasion must not be assumed from this biopsy.**
- Next steps:
  - Pre-operative estimate: pelvic MRI or expert transvaginal ultrasound.
  - Definitive depth and its ratio to myometrial thickness: measured on the hysterectomy specimen.

## KEY PROGNOSTIC FEATURES:

| Feature | Status from report | Effect on risk |
|---|---|---|
| Histotype | Endometrioid | Non-aggressive type (FIGO 2023); favourable |
| Grade | FIGO grade 2 (moderately differentiated) | Low grade; favourable |
| LVSI | Not identified in this sample | Favourable but provisional |
| Polyp involvement | Some polypoid fragments involved | Stage IA1 only if confined to polyp/endometrium on hysterectomy; not proven |
| Age | 47 years | Under 60, which matters for de-escalation if risk is intermediate. Diagnosis before 50 is a classic Lynch syndrome warning sign. |
| Molecular subgroup | **Unknown** | Main driver of risk: POLEmut makes stage I–II disease low risk; p53abn with any myometrial invasion becomes IICm p53abn (high risk) |
| ER/PR, β-catenin | **Unknown** | NSMP that is ER-negative with myometrial invasion is high risk despite low grade |
| Depth of myometrial invasion | **Unknown (not assessable)** | Separates IA from IB |
| Cervical stromal invasion | **Unknown** (no normal endocervix) | Would define IIA |
| LVSI extent (focal vs substantial) | **Unknown** | Substantial would mean IIB |
| Adnexa, serosa, nodes, peritoneum | **Unknown** (no staging or imaging) | Would define stage III–IV |

- **Sampling limitations:**
  - fragmented material (0.5 cc, 3 cc and 1 cc)
  - no myometrium
  - scarce basal endometrium
  - no normal endocervix
  - no separate microscopic description
  - no block-by-block distribution of the carcinoma
  - biopsy grade and histotype can change on the hysterectomy
- **ESGO-ESTRO-ESP 2025 risk group: cannot be allocated.** Allocation needs both the FIGO 2023 stage and the molecular subgroup. For this low-grade endometrioid tumour, the possible range runs from:
  - **low risk:** e.g., POLEmut stage I–II, or MMRd / NSMP-ER-positive stage IA
  - to **high risk:** e.g., p53abn or NSMP-ER-negative with myometrial invasion, or stage III–IVA in any subgroup other than POLEmut (POLEmut stage III–IVA is "uncertain risk")

## RECOMMENDED MANAGEMENT:
Neither the stage nor the molecular subgroup is known, so a definitive adjuvant plan cannot be set yet. The recommended sequence is: complete the molecular classification, stage the disease surgically, then treat according to the integrated risk group.

**1. Complete the pathology now (on Block 3, or Block 2 if Block 3 has too little tumour)**
- Perform the suggested IHC: p53, MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2, ER, PR and β-catenin, plus p16 and keratin cocktail as diagnostic aids.
- **Add POLE mutation testing.**
  - ESGO 2025 allows it to be omitted only in low-risk stage I disease, where the result would not change adjuvant treatment.
  - The stage is unknown, so testing is warranted.
  - A POLE wild-type result is also needed before a tumour can be called NSMP, or before p53abn can be accepted as the driver.
  - The result decides treatment if final pathology shows stage IB, cervical stromal invasion, substantial LVSI or p53abn with myometrial invasion; in those cases a POLE mutation would allow de-escalation to no adjuvant treatment.
- Test MLH1 promoter methylation if MLH1 (with or without PMS2) expression is lost.
- Molecular testing on curettage material is valid and encouraged. It only needs repeating on the hysterectomy if tumour is scant, results are equivocal, or a new tumour component appears.
- Ask the pathologist for an addendum that:
  - confirms "FIGO II" means grade 2
  - states which samples contain carcinoma, especially Block 1 ("Endocervix")
  - adds microscopic details

  Consider review by an expert gynaecological pathologist.
- HER2 testing is not indicated yet. It becomes relevant if the tumour proves p53-abnormal with advanced or recurrent disease, or if the histotype is revised to serous carcinoma or carcinosarcoma (ESGO 2025).

**2. Pre-operative work-up**
- History: family history of Lynch-associated cancers, menopausal status, comorbidities and reproductive wishes.
- Pelvic and speculum examination.
- Pelvic MRI (preferred here, to assess cervical stromal involvement and myometrial depth) or expert transvaginal ultrasound.
- Chest imaging. Consider CT of the abdomen and pelvis (or PET-CT) if there are high-risk molecular or imaging features, or suspicion of disease outside the uterus.

**3. Primary surgery (for presumed uterus-confined disease)**
- **Standard operation:** total (simple) hysterectomy with BSO and sentinel lymph node biopsy (indocyanine green by cervical injection, with ultrastaging of the nodes).
  - A minimally invasive approach is preferred.
  - Avoid morcellation and tumour spillage.
  - If sentinel nodes do not map, perform side-specific lymphadenectomy for high-intermediate or high risk, and consider it for intermediate risk.
- **Omentectomy:** not needed for endometrioid histology.
- **Radical hysterectomy:** not indicated because of "FIGO II", which is a grade, not a stage. If imaging shows cervical stromal invasion, more extensive surgery is justified only when needed to achieve clear margins.
- **Ovarian preservation:** ESGO 2025 limits it to premenopausal patients under 45 with FIGO 2023 IA1/IA2 disease that is low risk by molecular subgroup, with bilateral salpingectomy recommended. Ovaries should not be preserved in carriers of Lynch (MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2) or BRCA germline mutations. At 47 she falls outside the age criterion, so BSO is the standard (her menopausal status is not reported).
- **Fertility-sparing treatment:** no wish for it is documented. Under ESGO/ESHRE/ESGE 2023 it is standard only for grade 1, stage IA disease without myometrial invasion. For grade 2 it would be decided case by case in an expert centre, with a second pathology opinion.

**4. Adjuvant therapy, depending on final FIGO 2023 stage and molecular subgroup (ESGO-ESTRO-ESP 2025, low-grade endometrioid)**

| Final molecular subgroup | Final FIGO 2023 stage | Risk group | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|
| POLEmut | Any stage I–II (reported as IAm POLEmut) | Low | No adjuvant therapy |
| POLEmut | III–IVA | Uncertain | Decide case by case; de-escalation can be considered |
| MMRd | IA1 / IA2 / IA3 | Low | No adjuvant therapy |
| MMRd | IB | Intermediate | Consider vaginal brachytherapy (VBT); no adjuvant therapy is an option, especially under 60 |
| MMRd | IIA (cervical stroma) or IIB (substantial LVSI) | High-intermediate | External beam radiotherapy (EBRT). VBT is an alternative, especially if nodes are negative (pN0). Observation can be considered if pN0, no substantial LVSI and low grade. |
| MMRd | III–IVA | High | EBRT with concurrent and adjuvant chemotherapy, or sequential chemotherapy and radiotherapy. Chemotherapy with or without VBT is an alternative. Chemotherapy plus an immune checkpoint inhibitor (with or without EBRT) should be considered. |
| NSMP, ER-positive | IA1 / IA2 / IA3 | Low | No adjuvant therapy |
| NSMP, ER-positive | IB or IIA | Intermediate | Consider VBT; no adjuvant therapy is an option |
| NSMP, ER-positive | IIB | High-intermediate | EBRT; VBT is an alternative if pN0 |
| NSMP, ER-positive | III–IVA | High | Chemoradiotherapy or sequential chemotherapy and radiotherapy; chemotherapy with or without VBT |
| NSMP, ER-negative | IA1 | Uncertain | Adjuvant therapy generally not recommended |
| NSMP, ER-negative | IA2, IA3, IB, II, III–IVA | High | EBRT with chemotherapy (concurrent/adjuvant or sequential); chemotherapy with or without VBT is an alternative |
| p53abn | No myometrial invasion (polyp/endometrium only) | Uncertain | Adjuvant therapy generally not recommended |
| p53abn | Any myometrial invasion (IICm p53abn) or stage III–IVA | High | EBRT with concurrent and adjuvant chemotherapy, or sequential; chemotherapy with or without VBT is an alternative |
| Any | III–IVA with residual disease, IVB, IVC | Advanced | **MMRd:** carboplatin–paclitaxel plus an immune checkpoint inhibitor (dostarlimab, durvalumab or pembrolizumab), then maintenance immunotherapy. **Non-MMRd:** carboplatin–paclitaxel; chemo-immunotherapy followed by immunotherapy maintenance (± a PARP inhibitor, e.g., durvalumab + olaparib) can be considered. **Low-grade, ER-positive, low-volume or slowly progressing disease:** endocrine therapy (progestins) is preferred. |

**5. Genetics, follow-up and tumour board plan**
- If MMR deficiency is not explained by MLH1 promoter methylation, or the family history is suggestive, offer genetic counselling and germline testing for Lynch syndrome. This has consequences for surveillance, testing of relatives, and BSO rather than ovarian preservation.
- Follow-up should be tailored to the molecular subgroup and the treatment given. Inform the patient about specialised centres and clinical trials.
- **Re-present at tumour board twice:**
  1. after the IHC/POLE results and MRI, to plan surgery
  2. after final surgical pathology, to set the definitive FIGO 2023 stage, molecular annotation and adjuvant decision

2. **FIGO staging (2009 and 2023) is surgical-pathological.** It needs hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy (BSO) and nodal staging to define:
   - depth of myometrial invasion
   - cervical stromal invasion
   - extent of lymphovascular space invasion (LVSI): focal, or substantial (≥5 vessels)

anthropic/claude-opus-5.summary:
# Tumour Board Diagnostic Summary — Endometrial Pathology

**Report:** Anatomical Pathology Report – Histological Study, Request No. **2605694**
**Patient:** Female, **47 years** (anonymized), outpatient service
**Admission:** 05/07/2026 · **Report date:** 05/11/2026
**Specimens (3 samples, resection):**
- Block 1 — "Endocervix": mucohemorrhagic material, combined volume **0.5 cc**
- Block 2 — "Endometrium": mucohemorrhagic material, combined volume **3 cc**
- Block 3 — "Endometrial polyps": multiple light-brown tissue fragments with raw surfaces, combined volume **1 cc**

> **Critical framing for the board:** this is a **small-volume endometrial/endocervical resection–curettage specimen (total ≈4.5 cc, 3 blocks)**, *not* a hysterectomy. Microscopic description states only "See diagnosis." No myometrium, no uterine serosa, no adnexa, no parametria and no lymph nodes are present. Therefore several staging and risk parameters below are, by specimen type, **not assessable** rather than negative.

---

## DIAGNOSIS

**Endometrioid pattern endometrial adenocarcinoma, moderately differentiated — FIGO grade 2 (G2).**

Verbatim from the report:

> "ENDOCERVIX, ENDOMETRIUM, ENDOMETRIAL POLYPS, RESECTION (3 SAMPLES):
> – ENDOMETRIOID PATTERN ENDOMETRIAL ADENOCARCINOMA, MODERATELY DIFFERENTIATED, FIGO II, WITHOUT EVIDENCE OF VASCULONEURAL INVASION IN THIS SAMPLE.
> – SOME POLYPOID FRAGMENTS WITH ADENOCARCINOMA INVOLVEMENT.
> – NO NORMAL ENDOCERVIX IDENTIFIED.
> – SCARCE REPRESENTATION OF BASAL ENDOMETRIUM."

- **Histological type:** endometrioid adenocarcinoma (endometrioid pattern) — a *non-aggressive / low-grade* histotype in the WHO 5th edition and FIGO 2023 framework.
- **Grade:** **FIGO grade 2** (moderately differentiated). The report's "**FIGO II**" is a **grading** statement, not a stage: it is written in the same clause as, and as the numeric equivalent of, "MODERATELY DIFFERENTIATED," which is the definition of FIGO grade 2 (6–50% solid non-squamous/non-morular growth). It must **not** be transcribed into the tumour-board record as "FIGO stage II" — that would wrongly imply cervical stromal invasion, which is neither stated nor assessable here (see below).
- **Additional findings:** carcinoma involves **some of the polypoid fragments** (Block 3), i.e. the tumour has a documented polyp-associated component. **No normal endocervix was identified** in Block 1, and there is **scarce representation of basal endometrium** in the endometrial sampling.
- Not reported / not evaluable in this material: tumour size, unequivocal serous/clear-cell/undifferentiated or carcinosarcoma component (none described), MELF-type invasion, and background endometrium (hyperplasia/atypical hyperplasia not characterized).

---

## FIGO STAGE

**Cannot be assigned from this specimen — pathological (surgical) FIGO stage is indeterminate. Clinically the disease is presumed early-stage (cT1 Nx Mx) pending hysterectomy and imaging.**

Reasoning:
1. FIGO staging of endometrial carcinoma (both FIGO 2009 and FIGO 2023) is a **surgical–pathological** system requiring assessment of **myometrial invasion depth, cervical stromal involvement, serosa/adnexa, parametria, vagina, peritoneum and lymph nodes**. None of these structures is present in a 3-block endocervical/endometrial/polyp curettage–resection.
2. The specimen contains **no myometrium**; furthermore, "scarce representation of **basal endometrium**" means even the endometrial–myometrial junction is under-represented, so the endometrium-versus-myoinvasion question cannot be approached indirectly.
3. The "Endocervix" fraction is **non-informative** — "no normal endocervix identified" documents an inadequate/unrepresentative cervical sample. It **neither confirms nor excludes** cervical stromal invasion, and fractional curettage cannot reliably establish cervical stromal invasion in any case (contamination/false-positive and sampling false-negative both occur). Stage II therefore cannot be claimed on this material.
4. **Anticipated stage if hysterectomy confirms the current picture:** carcinoma limited to an endometrial polyp/endometrium with no LVSI in a grade 2 endometrioid (non-aggressive) tumour would correspond to **FIGO 2023 Stage IA1** (≈ FIGO 2009 Stage IA); <50% myometrial invasion would be **FIGO 2023 Stage IA2** (FIGO 2009 IA); ≥50% invasion would be **Stage IB**; cervical stromal invasion would be **Stage II**. This is an expectation, **not** an assigned stage.
5. Note also that **FIGO 2023 stage can be modified by molecular class** (e.g. *POLE*-mutated early-stage disease is down-staged to **IAm<sub>POLE-mut</sub>**; p53-abnormal disease with any myoinvasion is up-staged to **IICm<sub>p53abn</sub>**). Because the molecular class is unknown here (below), even a future stage assignment must be issued as molecularly-integrated only after the recommended testing.

---

## MOLECULAR SUBGROUP (WHO 5th edition integrated classification)

**Cannot be assigned — no molecular or immunohistochemical results are available. The subgroup is PENDING / UNCLASSIFIED (WHO "NSMP" must NOT be assigned by default).**

- The report's COMMENTS section only **suggests** testing: "On Block 3, immunohistochemistry studies are suggested, especially to determine biomarker profile including **Keratin Cocktail, P53, P16, Estrogen Receptors, Progesterone Receptors, Beta-Catenin, MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, and PMS2**." No stains were performed, and **no result** for any marker is reported.
- Consequently: **MMR status unknown** (MLH1/PMS2/MSH2/MSH6 not done), **p53 status unknown**, and ***POLE* status unknown** — no *POLE* exonuclease-domain sequencing is mentioned or recommended in the report, yet it is obligatory for the WHO/ProMisE algorithm.
- **NSMP is a diagnosis of exclusion** requiring a *POLE* wild-type, MMR-proficient, p53 wild-type result. With zero results in hand, defaulting to NSMP would be a category error; the honest classification is **"molecular subgroup not determined on available material."**
- **Feasibility:** the material is adequate in principle — the pathologist specifically nominated **Block 3 (endometrial polyps, 1 cc, carcinoma-involved)** for the panel, so IHC ± *POLE* sequencing can be run on existing blocks now, without re-biopsy, and repeated/confirmed later on the hysterectomy specimen.
- **Caveat for the board:** p53 and MMR IHC on curettage material is generally concordant with hysterectomy, so an early result is actionable for surgical planning; discordances (especially subclonal p53 and "multiple-classifier" tumours, where *POLE* takes precedence) should be resolved on the resection specimen.

---

## LYMPHOVASCULAR INVASION

**Not identified in the submitted material — reported as "WITHOUT EVIDENCE OF VASCULONEURAL INVASION IN THIS SAMPLE." This is a negative finding of limited value, not a validated "LVSI-absent" status.**

- The pathologist's own qualifier "**in this sample**" flags the sampling limitation.
- Curettage/resection fragments lack intact myometrial vasculature and the tumour–myometrium interface, where LVSI is normally detected; a negative result here has low negative predictive value.
- The FIGO 2023 / ESGO–ESTRO–ESP distinction between **focal** and **substantial (extensive) LVSI** — the parameter that actually drives adjuvant therapy and which up-stages non-aggressive tumours to **Stage IIB** when substantial — **cannot be evaluated** and must be re-assessed on the hysterectomy specimen.
- The wording "vasculoneural" also implies perineural invasion was not seen; likewise not assessable.

---

## MYOMETRIAL INVASION

**Not assessable — depth cannot be estimated from this specimen.**

- The macroscopic description lists only mucohemorrhagic material and polypoid tissue fragments (0.5 cc + 3 cc + 1 cc); **no myometrium was submitted or identified**, and the report makes no statement about myoinvasion.
- "**Scarce representation of basal endometrium**" explicitly documents that even the deep/basal endometrial compartment is poorly represented, further precluding any inference about the endomyometrial junction.
- The presence of "some polypoid fragments with adenocarcinoma involvement" raises but does **not** resolve the possibility of a polyp-confined (non-invasive) carcinoma; conversely, absence of myometrium in a curettage never excludes deep invasion.
- **Depth of invasion must be determined on the hysterectomy specimen** (with preoperative contrast-enhanced pelvic MRI as an interim estimate), reported as none / <50% / ≥50% of myometrial thickness.

---

## KEY PROGNOSTIC FEATURES

**Favourable / low-risk-leaning (from available data)**
- **Endometrioid histotype** — WHO "non-aggressive" (low-grade) histological type.
- **FIGO grade 2** (moderately differentiated) — intermediate, but still within the low-grade (G1–G2) category.
- **No LVSI (and no perineural invasion) identified** in the examined fragments.
- **Carcinoma involving endometrial polyps**, compatible with a possible polyp-confined/early tumour (would be FIGO 2023 IA1 if confirmed).
- **No serous, clear-cell, undifferentiated or sarcomatous component described**; no extrauterine disease documented in this material.

**Unfavourable / uncertainty-generating (drive the risk stratification gaps)**
- **Molecular class entirely unknown** — the single largest prognostic gap. p53-abnormal would convert this into high-risk disease even at an early stage (and up-stage it to IICm under FIGO 2023); *POLE*-ultramutated would make it excellent-prognosis and a de-escalation candidate; MMR-deficient carries intermediate prognosis plus **Lynch syndrome** and immunotherapy implications.
- **Myometrial invasion depth unknown**; **cervical stromal involvement unassessable** (Block 1 yielded no normal endocervix); **nodal status unknown**.
- **Grade 2 + curettage sampling** — grade is upgraded on hysterectomy in a non-trivial proportion of cases, and a high-grade or non-endometrioid component may still be revealed.
- **ER/PR status unknown** (recommended but not performed) — relevant to prognosis, to NSMP sub-stratification (ER-positive NSMP behaves better), and to any hormonal therapy option.
- **Negative LVSI is unreliable** in this specimen type, and **substantial vs focal LVSI** cannot be graded.
- **Age 47 (premenopausal)** — mandates Lynch syndrome consideration (age <50 with endometrial cancer), discussion of ovarian preservation/surgical menopause, and awareness of synchronous ovarian primaries in younger women with endometrioid carcinoma.

**Net assessment:** the data support a **low-grade, non-aggressive endometrioid endometrial carcinoma, most likely early-stage**, but a definitive ESGO/ESTRO/ESP risk group (low vs intermediate vs high-intermediate vs high) **cannot be assigned** until surgical staging and molecular classification are complete.

---

## RECOMMENDED MANAGEMENT

### 1. Complete the pathology work-up now (on existing blocks)
- Perform the **IHC panel recommended on Block 3**: **MLH1, PMS2, MSH2, MSH6** (MMR), **p53**, **ER, PR**, **beta-catenin**, **p16**, and **keratin cocktail** (the latter for confirmation of epithelial nature / assessment of invasion patterns and, with p16/ER, to help distinguish endometrial from endocervical origin given the non-representative endocervical block).
- **Add *POLE* exonuclease-domain sequencing (exons 9–14)** — not listed in the report but **mandatory** for the WHO 5th-edition/FIGO 2023 integrated classification and the only way to identify the de-escalation-eligible group.
- Apply the **ProMisE/WHO hierarchy**: *POLE*-mutated → MMR-deficient → p53-abnormal → NSMP, and report **multiple classifiers** by that precedence.
- **Reflex *MLH1* promoter hypermethylation** testing if MLH1/PMS2 loss is found; **germline testing / genetics referral** for unmethylated MLH1 loss or any MSH2/MSH6/PMS2 loss — reinforced by the patient's age of 47.

### 2. Staging work-up before surgery
- **Contrast-enhanced pelvic MRI** (best assessment of myometrial invasion depth and cervical stromal involvement — the two parameters left open by this specimen) plus **CT chest/abdomen/pelvis** (or PET-CT if extrauterine disease is suspected).
- Baseline **CA-125** (optional; useful if extrauterine disease suspected), and preoperative anaesthetic/comorbidity assessment.

### 3. Definitive surgery (the step that actually establishes the FIGO stage)
- **Total hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy**, preferably by **minimally invasive (laparoscopic/robotic) approach**, with **intact uterine removal** and avoidance of morcellation; **peritoneal assessment** with washings for cytology (recorded, though washings do not alter FIGO stage).
- **Bilateral sentinel lymph node mapping with ultrastaging** — appropriate for apparent early-stage disease; convert to full pelvic ± para-aortic lymphadenectomy only for failed mapping or per institutional protocol/high-risk findings.
- **Ovarian preservation:** generally **not** the default at age 47; bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy is recommended, with the option discussed individually only if disease proves grade 1–2, clinically confined to the uterus, without Lynch syndrome and without a family history of ovarian/breast cancer. **Bilateral salpingectomy at minimum** if ovaries are conserved. Counsel on surgical menopause and hormone-replacement options.
- **Fertility-sparing progestin therapy is NOT indicated** here: it is restricted to grade 1 endometrioid carcinoma with no myometrial invasion, and this tumour is **grade 2** with invasion status unknown. Primary progestin/levonorgestrel-IUD therapy would be reserved for patients medically unfit for surgery.

### 4. Adjuvant therapy — defer decision, then use molecularly integrated risk groups
No adjuvant recommendation can be finalized until final stage, grade, LVSI quantification and molecular class are available. Planned logic (ESGO/ESTRO/ESP, molecularly integrated):
- ***POLE*-ultramutated, early stage (I–II):** excellent prognosis — **omit adjuvant treatment** (de-escalation), observation only.
- **MMR-deficient, Stage IA–IB, grade 2, no/focal LVSI:** low to intermediate risk — **observation or vaginal brachytherapy**; MMR-d status also flags **Lynch syndrome screening** and makes **immune checkpoint inhibition** (e.g. pembrolizumab/dostarlimab with chemotherapy) the preferred option in the advanced/recurrent setting.
- **p53-abnormal with any myometrial invasion:** high risk (**FIGO 2023 Stage IICm**) — **adjuvant chemotherapy (carboplatin–paclitaxel) ± external beam radiotherapy**; consider **HER2 testing** and trastuzumab-containing strategies if a serous-like/HER2-positive phenotype emerges.
- **NSMP (if confirmed):** manage by classical pathology — **Stage IA, G2, LVSI-negative → low risk, observation** (vaginal brachytherapy optional, more so if age >60); **Stage IB or substantial LVSI or cervical stromal invasion → intermediate/high-intermediate risk → vaginal brachytherapy ± external beam radiotherapy**, with chemotherapy added for high-risk/advanced disease. ER/PR positivity supports endocrine options in the recurrent setting.

### 5. Multidisciplinary and supportive measures
- **Re-present at the gynae-oncology tumour board** once the hysterectomy pathology, sentinel node ultrastaging and the molecular panel are reported, to issue a **definitive molecularly integrated FIGO 2023 stage and risk group**.
- **Genetic counselling referral** if MMR-deficient/Lynch-suspicious, with cascade testing and colorectal/gastric surveillance as indicated.
- **Menopausal symptom management**, bone health, sexual health/vaginal dilator counselling if pelvic radiotherapy is used, and **weight/metabolic risk optimization** (obesity, diabetes, hypertension are standard endometrioid carcinoma co-factors — not documented in this report).
- **Surveillance** after treatment: symptom-directed clinical review every 3–6 months for 2–3 years, then 6–12 monthly to 5 years; imaging as clinically indicated. Counsel on postmenopausal/abnormal bleeding as the key recurrence symptom.

---

## Summary Table

| Field | Answer | Basis / limitation |
|---|---|---|
| **Diagnosis** | Endometrioid adenocarcinoma of endometrium, moderately differentiated, **FIGO grade 2**; involves endometrial polyp fragments | Report diagnosis line; "FIGO II" = **grade** 2, not stage |
| **FIGO stage** | **Not assignable** (indeterminate); clinically presumed early-stage cT1 Nx Mx; would be FIGO 2023 IA1 if polyp/endometrium-confined at hysterectomy | Curettage/resection specimen, 3 blocks, ≈4.5 cc; no myometrium, cervix stroma, adnexa or nodes |
| **Molecular subgroup** | **Cannot be assigned — pending**. Not NSMP by default | IHC only *suggested* on Block 3; no results; no *POLE* testing ordered |
| **Lymphovascular invasion** | **Not identified** ("no evidence of vasculoneural invasion **in this sample**") — unreliable negative; focal vs substantial LVSI not evaluable | Pathologist's own qualifier; specimen type |
| **Myometrial invasion** | **Not assessable** — no myometrium present; "scarce representation of basal endometrium" | Macroscopic description; no myoinvasion statement |
| **Key prognostic features** | Favourable: endometrioid type, G2, no LVSI seen, polyp involvement. Unfavourable/unknown: molecular class, invasion depth, cervical/nodal status, ER/PR, age 47 (Lynch screening) | Report content + specimen limitations |
| **Recommended management** | Complete IHC (MMR, p53, ER/PR, p16, beta-catenin, keratin) **+ *POLE* sequencing** on Block 3; pelvic MRI + CT; total hysterectomy + BSO with sentinel node mapping/ultrastaging; adjuvant therapy decided afterwards by molecularly integrated FIGO 2023 stage/ESGO risk group; Lynch screening/genetics | Standard of care applied to reported findings |

**Bottom line for the board:** a histologically confirmed **FIGO grade 2 endometrioid endometrial adenocarcinoma involving endometrial polyps, with no LVSI seen in a limited curettage/resection sample**. The report supplies a **grade, not a stage** — "FIGO II" must be recorded as grade 2 — and the **FIGO stage, myometrial invasion depth and molecular subgroup are all currently undeterminable**. Surgical staging plus the recommended IHC panel with added *POLE* sequencing are the two actions that will convert this into a fully classified, treatment-defining diagnosis.
